key_findings: Unbacked RWX memory region discovered inside powershell.exe (PID 2844) executing reflective Cobalt Strike beacon.
Process hollowing and Parent-PID spoofing detected: svchost.exe (PID 3000) was spawned by explorer.exe instead of services.exe.
Stealth rootkit identified: rootkit_stealth.exe (PID 6666) unlinked from ActiveProcessLinks (DKOM) while running 8 active threads.
Encrypted Command & Control (C2) beaconing observed targeting external endpoint 198.51.100.44:443.
Kernel SSDT and driver signature verification confirmed zero hypervisor-level compromises (Scope restricted to OS level).
summary.business_impact: Critical compromise of endpoint integrity and confidentiality. Active memory persistence and C2 beaconing indicate ongoing hands-on-keyboard adversary access capable of data exfiltration and domain privilege escalation.
immediate_actions: Immediately isolate target endpoint host (DESKTOP-EXECUTIVE) from local network and active directory domain.
Revoke and rotate Kerberos TGT and NTLM credentials for user account 'Finance_Executive' and Domain Admin accounts.
Block network communication to external IP 198.51.100.44 and domain telemetry.msupdate-cloud.com across perimeter firewalls.

findings.title: Unbacked Executable Memory Injection (Cobalt Strike Beacon)
findings.description: Forensic inspection of powershell.exe (PID: 2844) identified an anomalous Virtual Address Descriptor (VAD) region configured with PAGE_EXECUTE_READWRITE permissions. The region lacks any backing image on physical disk (private memory) and contains a reflective DLL loader, followed by a Cobalt Strike HTTPS beaconing loop communicating with remote address 198.51.100.44:443.

artifacts.disassembly:
0x000001D48A201080:  push rbp
0x000001D48A201081:  mov rbp, rsp
0x000001D48A201084:  sub rsp, 0x20
0x000001D48A201088:  call 0x000001D48A201200  ; ReflectiveLoader API Resolution
0x000001D48A20108D:  mov rax, qword ptr [rbp-0x10]
0x000001D48A201091:  jmp rax                     ; Jump to Decrypted Stage

reasoning: Identified process powershell.exe containing VAD allocation with PAGE_EXECUTE_READWRITE permissions.
Verified through memory-mapped file handles that region 0x000001D48A200000 has NO backing file on physical storage.
Disassembly proves valid x86_64 machine code beginning with reflective shellcode preamble.
Corroborated active execution thread (TID 3012) executing within this unbacked address space.
Tri-State Verdict: TRUE (Malicious In-Memory Execution Confirmed).
remediation: Blackhole C2 destination 198.51.100.44 and domain telemetry.msupdate-cloud.com on network perimeter.
Deploy EDR memory-scan policy across all endpoints in the financial subnet.
findings.why_it_matters: RWX memory allocation is standard for Cobalt Strike and reflective DLL loaders because it allows an attacker to write encoded payloads into RAM and immediately execute them without calling disk-backed file APIs, evading disk-based antivirus scanners.

findings.title: Process Hollowing & Lineage Spoofing in svchost.exe
findings.description: Process svchost.exe (PID: 3000) was detected with a compromised PE header in its primary image base (0x00007FF71A400000). The executable section exhibits private modified memory regions replacing legitimate svchost binary code. Furthermore, its parent process ID points to explorer.exe (PID: 1420) instead of services.exe.

artifacts.disassembly:
0x00007FF71A402400:  sub rsp, 0x28
0x00007FF71A402404:  mov rdx, 0x7ff71a403000   ; Injected Payload Base
0x00007FF71A40240B:  call 0x7ff71a402910       ; Decryption Stub
0x00007FF71A402410:  add rsp, 0x28
0x00007FF71A402414:  ret

reasoning: Cross-referenced PID 3000 against standard Windows service hosting parent rules.
Confirmed PPID 1420 (explorer.exe) violates mandatory services.exe parenthood.
Calculated discrepancy between disk image hash and in-memory image base hash.
Detected unbacked RWX VAD overwriting legitimate PE code section.
remediation: Isolate user session 1 for forensic endpoint triage.
Audit explorer.exe memory space for injection triggers.
findings.why_it_matters: Process hollowing allows malware to borrow the identity of a trusted Windows binary, confusing security analysts and bypassing firewalls that trust svchost.exe network activity.

findings.title: Direct Kernel Object Manipulation (DKOM) Unlinked Rootkit
findings.description: Cross-table correlation between the active process doubly-linked list (pslist) and physical pool tag carving (psscan) unmasked an unlinked process: rootkit_stealth.exe (PID: 6666). The process was detached from ActiveProcessLinks to evade detection by Task Manager and API-based forensic tools, but continues active execution with 8 scheduled threads.
reasoning: Traversed PsActiveProcessHead linked list; PID 6666 was completely absent.
Scanned physical memory pools for 'Proc' tag structures; found intact EPROCESS for PID 6666.
Verified thread scheduler table; 8 threads remain actively dispatched by CPU.
Absence in pslist combined with presence in psscan proves intentional list unlinking (DKOM).
remediation: Acquire immediate full physical crash dump for kernel-mode debugger analysis.
Execute emergency system reboot to sever unlinked kernel memory execution.
Inspect kernel driver load logs in event viewer for unauthorized .sys drivers.
findings.why_it_matters: DKOM rootkits manipulate kernel structures directly. Standard antivirus scanners and forensic tools that rely on the Windows API cannot see unlinked processes, giving attackers persistent stealth control.

findings.title: Reflective DLL Injection & Named Pipe Inter-Process Hijack
findings.description: Analysis of the Print Spooler service (spoolsv.exe, PID: 1820) revealed an injected reflective DLL hosting a named pipe server (\\.\pipe\ms_spool_ipc_32). The payload is used to relay lateral commands between the unlinked rootkit and user-mode interactive sessions.
reasoning: Audited handle table for spoolsv.exe; identified uncataloged named pipe \\.\pipe\ms_spool_ipc_32.
Traced pipe handler to unbacked memory region 0x0000024B10000000.
Corroborated execution thread dispatched inside private memory space.
remediation: Restart Print Spooler service to terminate rogue thread.
Block named pipe creation via host hardening policy.
findings.why_it_matters: Named pipes are frequently used by fileless malware for stealthy inter-process communication (IPC) and lateral movement across systems without triggering network intrusion alerts.

limitations: Volatile memory analysis represents a snapshot in time; ephemeral network packets in transit prior to capture may not be recoverable.
Physical memory smear may occur when imaging active RAM on live systems due to CPU thread execution during acquisition.
Data pages swapped out to pagefile.sys or swapfile.sys on disk were not included in physical RAM acquisition.
Tri-State UNKNOWN findings reflect localized telemetry constraints and require external endpoint correlation before clearance.
